SafeOpenTool.name: safe_open_tool
SafeOpenTool.description:
This is a tool that opens a file replacing open().
                     It enforces security by forcing file access to occur strictly within the designated safe directory.
                     Any directory paths provided in 'file_name' will be stripped.

file_name.description: The name of the file to be opened. directory components are ignored; the file is looked up in the safe directory.

mode.description: 'rt' for text files, 'rb' for binary files (pdf, docx...)

AudioHandlerTool.name: audio_handler_tool
AudioHandlerTool.description:
This tool loads and saves .wav or .flac audio files within designated secure directories.

    Operations:
    - 'read': Returns a dictionary containing 'audio_samples' (as a numpy array) and 'metadata'.
      Reads strictly from the READ directory.
    - 'write': Saves a numpy array of audio samples to a file with specific quantization.
      Writes strictly to the WRITE directory.

    IMPORTANT: The 'read' output contains raw massive arrays. NEVER try to print the return value
    of this tool as an agent action or in the final answer. Always assign it to a variable.

file_name.description: The name of the file (wav/flac). Directory components are stripped.

audio_data.description: For 'write' mode only. A numpy array containing the audio samples.

sample_rate.description: For 'write' mode only. The sampling rate of the audio.

quantization.description: Bit depth for saving files. Allowed: [16, 24, 32] for .wav, [16, 24] for .flac.

TFDTool.name: time_frequency_distribution_tool
TFDTool.description:
Computes Time-Frequency Distributions (Cohen's Class) or Time-Scale Distributions (Affine Class).

    Supported Methods:
    - 'wvd': Wigner-Ville (Standard, high resolution)
    - 'choi_williams': Reduces interference (good for speech/bio)
    - 'rihaczek': Complex energy distribution
    - 'born_jordan': Preserves time support
    - 'zam': Cone-shaped kernel (ZAM), good for non-stationary
    - 'bertrand': Unitary Affine (Hyperbolic chirps)
    - 'unterberger': Active Wideband
    - 'affine': Scalogram analysis (Wavelet-like)

    Input: Requires the dictionary output from AudioHandlerTool.
    Output: Generates an ACTIVE Matplotlib figure. Returns a recommendation to use 'save_plot' or the raw data for advanced post-processing.

audio_dict.description: The dictionary returned by AudioHandlerTool (must contain 'audio_samples' and 'metadata').

channel.description: Channel index to analyze if audio is multi-channel. Default 0.

param.description: Kernel parameter (Sigma for Choi-Williams, Alpha for Bertrand/ZAM). Default varies by method.

start_sample.description: The starting sample index for the analysis window. Default is 0.

end_sample.description: The ending sample index for the analysis window. If None, uses the end of the signal.

force_computation.description: If True, overrides the O(N^2) complexity safety check for long signals (>3000 samples). Default is False.

return_data.description: If True, returns a dictionary with raw matrix and axes instead of saving a plot. Default False.

TFDDataTool.name: tfd_data_tool
TFDDataTool.description:
Manages the storage and retrieval of raw Time-Frequency Analysis data.
    - 'save': Saves the TFD data dictionary to a compressed .npz file.
    - 'load': Loads a .npz file back into a dictionary for processing.

data_dict.description: The dictionary returned by TFDTool (required for 'save').

LogFreqPlotTool.name: log_freq_plot_tool
LogFreqPlotTool.description:
Generates a Log-Frequency (Octave-scale) Spectrogram from raw TFD data.
    Useful for visualizing musical tones, speech, or wideband signals.
    Resamples the linear Time-Frequency matrix onto a logarithmic frequency grid.

    Returns a recommendation to use 'save_plot'.

tfd_data.description: The dictionary containing 'tfd_matrix' and 'axes' (from TFDTool or TFDDataTool).

f_min.description: Minimum frequency for the log axis (Hz). Default 20.

num_bins.description: Height of the resulting image in pixels/bins. Default 500.

EMDTool.name: emd_tool
EMDTool.description: Performs Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) on a specific audio channel. Returns a 2D NumPy array of the Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). The output shape is (number_of_samples, number_of_imfs).

audio_dict.description: The dictionary returned by AudioHandlerTool (containing 'audio_samples' and 'metadata').

channel.description: The channel index to analyze if audio is multi-channel. Default is 0.

max_imfs.description: Optional: The maximum number of IMFs to extract.

EMDToolGv2.name: emd_tool
EMDToolGv2.description: Performs Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) on a specific audio channel. Returns a 2D NumPy array of the Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). The output shape is (number_of_samples, number_of_imfs).

audio_dict.description: The dictionary returned by AudioHandlerTool (containing 'audio_samples' and 'metadata').

channel.description: The channel index to analyze if audio is multi-channel. Default is 0.

max_imfs.description: Optional: The maximum number of IMFs to extract.

CreateChromaDBTool.name: create_chromadb
CreateChromaDBTool.description: Creates a new, empty ChromaDB vector database at a specified path. If a database already exists at the path, it will be removed and replaced.

db_path.description: The file system path where the ChromaDB database will be created. Defaults to './chroma_db_mem0'.

embedder_model.description: The sentence-transformer model to configure for the database. Defaults to 'sentence-transformers/distiluse-base-multilin…

PopulateChromaDBTool.name: populate_chromadb
PopulateChromaDBTool.description: Reads a markdown dialog file, extracts memories using an LLM, and populates a specified ChromaDB collection with those memories.

db_path.description: Path to the ChromaDB database to populate.

markdown_file.description: Path to the markdown dialog file containing the conversation.

collection_name.description: The name of the collection to add the memories to.

user_id.description: A user ID to be stored in the metadata for each memory.

embedder_model.description: The sentence-transformer model to use for embedding. Defaults to 'sentence-transformers/distiluse-base-multilingual-case…

QueryChromaDBTool.name: query_chromadb
QueryChromaDBTool.description: Queries a ChromaDB database. It can perform several actions: 'list_collections': Lists all available collections. 'get_all_memories': Retrieves all memories from a specific collection. 'search': Performs a similarity search for a query within a collection.

db_path.description: Path to the ChromaDB database to query.

action.description: The action to perform. Supported values: 'list_collections', 'get_all_memories', 'search'.

collection_name.description: The name of the collection for 'get_all_memories' and 'search' actions.

query_text.description: The search query text for the 'search' action.

n_results.description: The number of results to return for a 'search' action. Defaults to 5.

embedder_model.description: The sentence-transformer model for embedding the search query. Defaults to 'sentence-transformers/distiluse-base-multili…

ManageChromaDBTool.name: manage_chromadb
ManageChromaDBTool.description: Manages a ChromaDB database with query and delete functions. Query actions: 'list_collections', 'get_all_memories', 'search'. Delete actions: 'delete_collection', 'delete_memories_by_ids', 'delete_memories_by_metadata'.

db_path.description: Path to the ChromaDB database to manage.

action.description: The action to perform. See tool description for supported actions.

collection_name.description: The target collection name. Required for most actions.

query_text.description: The search query text for the 'search' action.

n_results.description: Number of results for 'search' action. Defaults to 5.

memory_ids.description: A list of memory string IDs to delete. Required for 'delete_memories_by_ids'.

metadata_filter.description: A dictionary for metadata filtering (e.g., {'user_id': 'alice'}). Required for 'delete_memories_by_metadata'.

embedder_model.description: The sentence-transformer model for search query embedding. Defaults to 'sentence-transformers/distiluse-base-multilingua…

AnalyzeChromaDBTool.name: analyze_chromadb
AnalyzeChromaDBTool.description: Finds and verifies mem0 ChromaDB structures. Actions: 'find' to search for potential databases in a path, 'verify' to check if a specific path is a valid ChromaDB structure.

search_path.description: The directory path to start the search from (for 'find' action).

db_path.description: The path to a potential ChromaDB directory to verify (for 'verify' action).

MyGoogleSearchTool.name: web_search
MyGoogleSearchTool.description: Performs a web search based on your query (think a Google search) then returns the top search results.

SearXNGSearchTool.name: web_searXNG
SearXNGSearchTool.description: Performs a web search based on your query (think a Google search) then returns the top search results.

PrologTool.name: prolog_tool
PrologTool.description: Interface to SWI-Prolog. Supports consulting facts/rules, running queries, clearing the knowledge base, saving/loading KB to/from files, and auto-saving on close. File operations are restricted to a safe directory.

query_string.description: Prolog query to execute. Required for 'query'.

find_all.description: For 'query': return all solutions (True) or just the first (False).

reset_on_query.description: If True, resets the KB before each query.

reset_on_consult.description: If True, resets the KB before consulting new facts/rules.

reset_on_all.description: If True, resets the KB before BOTH consult and query.

save_to.description: Path to save the current KB (Prolog .pl file). Will be saved inside the safe directory.

load_from.description: Path to load a KB from a Prolog .pl file. Must exist inside the safe directory.

PDFSplitterToolGv1.name: pdf_splitter_tool
PDFSplitterToolGv1.description:
This tool extracts text from a PDF (local or URL) and splits it into Markdown files.
                     It preserves formatting and tables. Files are saved in the safe directory.

file_name.description: The pathname or URL of the PDF file to be split.

pages_per_chunk.description: Maximum number of pages per generated Markdown file.

PDFSplitterToolGv2.name: pdf_splitter_tool
PDFSplitterToolGv2.description:
Splits a PDF into Markdown files. It ensures chunks do not break
                     in the middle of a paragraph by splitting at double newlines.

file_name.description: The pathname or URL of the PDF file to be split.

pages_per_chunk.description: Maximum number of pages per generated Markdown file.

PDF2TXTTool.name: pdf_2_txt_tool
PDF2TXTTool.description:
This is a tool that extracts the text from a PDF file.
                     If the file is not in a safe directory it raises an exception.

file_name.description: The pathname or URL of the PDF file to be opened.

PDFAnalyzerTool.name: pdf_analyzer_tool
PDFAnalyzerTool.description:
Analyzes a PDF file to determine the best text extraction method (direct vs. OCR).
                     It provides a detailed report on text content, images, and text readability.
                     The file must be located in the secure upload directory.

pdf_filename.description: The name of the PDF file (e.g., 'report.pdf') located in the safe upload directory.

min_readable_ratio.description: The minimum ratio of readable characters (0.0 to 1.0) to consider text directly extractable. Defaults to 0.7.

sample_pages.description: The number of pages to sample for a quick analysis of large documents. Defaults to 3.

OCR2TXTTool.name: ocr_2_txt_tool
OCR2TXTTool.description:
Extracts text from PDF files using Optical Character Recognition (OCR).
                     This tool is essential for scanned documents, PDFs containing only images, or when PDFAnalyzerTool recommends 'OCR_REQUIRED' or 'HYBRID'.
                     It is more resource-intensive than the standard pdf_2_txt_tool.
                     The file must be located in the secure upload directory.

file_name.description: The name of the PDF file (e.g., 'scanned_report.pdf') located in the safe upload directory.

language.description: The language of the text in the document (e.g., 'eng' for English, 'ita' for Italian, 'fra' for French). Defaults to 'en…

CSV2TUPTool.name: csv_2_tup_tool
CSV2TUPTool.description:
This is a tool that extracts a tuple from a CSV file.
                     If the file is not in a safe directory it raises an exception.

file_name.description: The name of the file to be opened.

LLM_Tool.name: llm_tool
LLM_Tool.description: This is a tool that accepts a question (and possibly a list of images) and returns an answer.

question.description: The question to be answered. If it contains web URLs pointing to images, they must be explored with this tool, rather th…

list_of_images.description: An optional list, possibly empty, containing a mix of base64-encoded .JPG or .PNG images, paths to local image files, an…

Summarization_Tool.name: summarization_tool
Summarization_Tool.description: This is a tool that summarizes the input (a long multi-line string)

Translation_Tool.name: translation_tool
Translation_Tool.description: This is a tool that translates the input (a long multi-line string) from one language to another.

original_language.description: The original language of the text.

target_language.description: The target language for the translation.

MarkdownToPDFTool.name: markdown_to_pdf_tool
MarkdownToPDFTool.description:
Converts a given Markdown string into a PDF file.
                     It allows specifying the paper size, page orientation, and margin.
                     The resulting PDF is saved in a secure directory.

markdown_content.description: The Markdown content to be converted into a PDF.

output_filename.description: The desired filename for the output PDF (e.g., 'report.pdf'). It must end with .pdf.

paper_format.description: The paper size. Common values are 'a4', 'a3', 'letter', 'legal', 'a5'. Defaults to 'a4'.

orientation.description: The page orientation. Must be either 'portrait' or 'landscape'. Defaults to 'portrait'.

margin.description: The page margin as a string (e.g., '1in', '2cm', '0.75in'). Defaults to '1in'.

ArtifactVaultToolGv10.name: artifact_vault
ArtifactVaultToolGv10.description: A persistent HDF5 repository. Supports 'stash', 'retrieve', 'catalog', and 'update'. Retrieval is 'Flattened': for complex artifacts (like EMD), you can access signals directly via keys like result['original_signal'] or result['imf_matrix'].

data.description: Data to stash (Numpy array). Not needed for 'update'.

access_hint.description: Instructional Manual: What the data represents and how to index it.

ArtifactVaultToolGv16.name: artifact_vault
ArtifactVaultToolGv16.description:
A unified HDF5 repository for DSP data. Supports four actions:
- 'catalog': Returns a lite list of all artifact IDs.
- 'inspect': Returns deep metadata and shapes for a specific ID or wildcard pattern (e.g. 'EMD*').
- 'retrieve': Returns the data. Complex artifacts (EMD) are 'Flattened' for direct access to signals.
- 'stash': Saves numpy arrays or dictionaries with metadata into the vault.- 'audit': Scans all artifacts matching a prefix and returns a summary of their dataset shapes.    Use 'audit' for global complexity analysis without looping manually.

artifact_id.description: Unique ID or pattern (required for retrieve, stash, inspect).

data.description: Data to stash (Numpy array or dict).

access_hint.description: Stash only: Instructions on what the data represents.

ArtifactVaultInspectorToolGv2.name: artifact_inspector
ArtifactVaultInspectorToolGv2.description: Inspects the internal structure of the HDF5 vault. Returns a tree-like summary of artifact IDs, dataset shapes, dtypes, and metadata. Essential for 'scouting' the vault before retrieving large arrays.

vault_filename.description: The name of the vault file (default: 'research_session.h5').

ArtifactVaultInspectorToolGv3.name: artifact_inspector
ArtifactVaultInspectorToolGv3.description: Inspects the vault. If 'artifact_id' is omitted, returns a lite list of IDs. If 'artifact_id' is provided, returns deep metadata, shapes, and protocol hints for matching items. Use this to scout data before retrieval.

artifact_id.description: Optional: Specific ID or wildcard (e.g., 'EMD*') for deep inspection.

ArtifactVaultByPatternToolGv1.name: artifact_by_pattern
ArtifactVaultByPatternToolGv1.description: Inspects the HDF5 vault. If 'artifact_id' is provided, it returns deep shapes and metadata for that specific item. If 'artifact_id' is omitted, it returns a high-level summary of all available IDs to save context space.

artifact_id.description: Optional: Specific ID or prefix (e.g., 'MLSESS_IMFs_Seg_1*') to inspect.

vault_filename.description: The name of the vault file.

SlamFssSifterToolGv1.name: slam_fss_sifter
SlamFssSifterToolGv1.description: High-performance windowed EMD sifter. Loads a signal, applies a Tukey window, performs EMD, and stashes results in the hdf5_physics_archive automatically. Designed to prevent context overflow during massive 4M sample sweeps.

SlamFssSifterToolGv3.name: slam_fss_sifter
SlamFssSifterToolGv3.description: High-performance windowed EMD sifter. (S)elf-(A)ware of (R)ussian (D)olls: automatically unpacks nested audio dicts. If the signal is too short for multiple windows, it processes a single full-length window.

audio_dict.description: The dictionary returned by audio_handler_tool or artifact_vault.

PulseMatchToolV1.name: pulse_match_tool
PulseMatchToolV1.description: High-speed temporal synchronization tool. Finds a pulse template (Time Code) within a long signal using normalized cross-correlation. Returns indices, time-drift (remainder vs Fs), and correlation coefficients.

signal_id.description: Vault ID of the long signal (DUT output).

pulse_id.description: Vault ID of the pulse template (Dirac pair).

threshold.description: Correlation threshold (e.g., 0.99) to define a match.

SyncAlignmentToolV1.name: sync_alignment_tool
SyncAlignmentToolV1.description: Corrects manual alignment errors between MATLAB reference (L) and ADC capture (R). Finds the precise sample lag and returns a 'Realigned' view of the signal.

search_window_ms.description: Window to search for alignment (e.g., 5.0 for 5ms).

SyncAlignmentToolV2.name: sync_alignment_tool
SyncAlignmentToolV2.description: Precision alignment tool. Uses the SECOND Dirac pulse as a Master Anchor to avoid boundary effects at the signal origin. Corrects manual alignment errors between Ref (L) and DUT (R).

SavePlotTool.name: save_plot
SavePlotTool.description: Saves the currently active Matplotlib plot to a file in the secure 'plots' directory.

output_filename.description: The desired filename for the output PNG.

RVGTool.name: random_variate_generator
RVGTool.description: Generates lists of pseudo-random numbers from specified statistical distributions. It uses a high-precision Linear Congruential Generator (LCG) as its foundation. Available distributions: 'uniform', 'normal', 'exponential'.

distribution.description: The name of the probability distribution to sample from. Supported: 'uniform', 'normal', 'exponential'.

size.description: The number of random numbers to generate.

seed.description: An integer used to initialize the random number generator. Using the same seed will produce the exact same sequence of n…

distribution_params.description: A dictionary of parameters specific to the chosen distribution. For 'normal', use {'mu': <mean>, 'sigma': <standard_devi…

LCSAnalyzerTool.name: lcs_analyzer
LCSAnalyzerTool.description: Calculates the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) of two input texts. It first normalizes the texts by converting them into a sequence of root words using either lemmatization or stemming. Then, it uses an efficient algorithm to find the longest sequence of words common to both texts.

text1.description: The first text to be analyzed.

text2.description: The second text to be analyzed.

use_lemmatization.description: If True (default), uses lemmatization for text normalization. If False, uses stemming.

parallel.description: If True (default), processes the two texts in parallel to speed up normalization.

return_sequence.description: If True (default), returns the actual LCS sequence of words. If False, returns only its length.

ListBPFunctionsTool.name: list_bulletproof_functions
ListBPFunctionsTool.description:
Lists all available standard optimization functions stored in the internal BULLETPROOF library.
    Use this to discover available test functions (like 'mogadish', 'schwefel', 'cross_in_tray')
    before running an optimizer.

verbose.description: If True (default), returns details (bounds, global min, description). If False, returns only names.

GetBPFunctionCodeTool.name: get_bulletproof_function_code
GetBPFunctionCodeTool.description:
Retrieves the raw Python source code for a specific function from the BULLETPROOF library.
    Use this when you need to inspect the code, modify it (e.g., convert 'numpy' logic to 'mpmath'),
    or pass it to a tool that doesn't support automatic lookup.

function_name.description: The name of the function to retrieve (e.g., 'mogadish', 'rastrigin').

SimAnnealTool.name: simulated_annealing_optimizer
SimAnnealTool.description:
Finds the global minimum using Simulated Annealing v2.
    Returns the solution and saves history to a CSV.

    STANDARD FUNCTIONS:
    You can simply pass the name of a standard function in 'function_code' (e.g., "ackley", "rastrigin", "rosenbrock").
    This will use pre-validated code and bounds.

    CUSTOM FUNCTIONS:
    Pass the full Python code definition: "def objective(x): return ...".

    CRITICAL:
    The CSV is saved in a secure area. The Plotter cannot read it directly.
    You must read the data using `csv_2_tup_tool` and INJECT the lists into the plotting code.

function_code.description: Either the Python code defining 'def objective(x): ...' OR the name of a standard test function (e.g., 'rastrigin').

bounds.description: List of tuples for min/max per dimension. Optional if using a standard function name.

output_filename.description: Filename for history CSV (e.g., 'run1.csv'). Ends in .csv.

restart_stagnation.description: If provided, restarts/reheats after N iterations without improvement. (e.g., 500).

adapt_neighbor.description: If True (default), automatically adjusts step size. If False, uses fixed scale.

SAAnalysisTool.name: sa_analysis_tool
SAAnalysisTool.description:
Advanced analysis of Simulated Annealing history CSV.
    Detects convergence issues, acceptance problems, stagnation patterns,
    and gives precise, actionable tuning recommendations (v3 — fully upgraded).
    Supports all v2+ features: adaptive scaling, restarts, temperature logging.

csv_filename.description: Name of the history CSV file (e.g., 'run1.csv')

SimAnnealToolMP.name: simulated_annealing_mp
SimAnnealToolMP.description:
High-Precision Simulated Annealing (Arbitrary Precision).
    Uses 'mpmath' (mp) instead of 'numpy'.

    CRITICAL:
    1. The 'function_code' MUST be written for mpmath (e.g. `mp.sin`, `mp.sqrt`, `mp.mpf`).
    2. Use `get_bulletproof_function_code` to retrieve pre-written MP code (e.g. 'mogadish_mp').
    3. `dps` sets the decimal places (e.g. 50, 100).

function_code.description: Python code defining 'def objective(x): ...' using mpmath.

bounds.description: List of tuples e.g. '[(-1, 1)]' (passed as string literal).

max_iterations.description: Default 1000. Keep low for MP speed.

GATool.name: genetic_algorithm_optimizer
GATool.description:
Finds the global minimum using a Real-Coded Genetic Algorithm.
    Useful for multimodal functions where Simulated Annealing might get stuck.

    OUTPUT:
    - Returns best solution.
    - Saves history to CSV (Generation, Best Energy, Diversity).

    CRITICAL:
    Read CSV using `csv_2_tup_tool` and INJECT data into `python_plotter`.

function_code.description: Python code 'def objective(x): ...' OR a standard function name (e.g., 'rastrigin', 'schwefel').

bounds.description: Bounds e.g. [(-5, 5)]. Optional if using a standard function name.

GAAnalysisTool.name: ga_analysis_tool
GAAnalysisTool.description:
Analyzes 'history.csv' from the Genetic Algorithm.
    Diagnoses 'Premature Convergence' by looking at Population Diversity vs Energy.

csv_filename.description: Name of the history CSV file.

GAToolMP.name: genetic_algorithm_mp
GAToolMP.description:
High-Precision Genetic Algorithm (Arbitrary Precision).
    Uses 'mpmath' instead of 'numpy'. Best for resolving 'Planck-scale' features.

    CRITICAL:
    1. The 'function_code' MUST be written for mpmath (e.g. `mp.sin`).
    2. Use `get_bulletproof_function_code` or standard names (e.g., 'mogadish_mp').
    3. `dps` sets the decimal places (e.g. 50, 100).

function_code.description: Python code 'def objective(x): ...' OR standard name.

bounds.description: Bounds e.g. [(-0.1, 0.1)]. Optional if using standard name.

DEToolMP.name: differential_evolution_mp
DEToolMP.description: High-precision Differential Evolution with Island Model using pure mpmath.

function_code.description: A string of Python code defining the objective function to be minimized. The function must be named 'objective' and acce…

bounds.description: A list of tuples, where each tuple defines the lower and upper bounds for a dimension. Example: [(-5, 5), (-5, 5)]

output_filename.description: The base filename for the output CSV and plot files. Must end with .csv.

dps.description: Decimal Precision Setting (dps) for mpmath arbitrary-precision calculations. Default is 50.

num_islands.description: The number of separate populations (islands) to evolve. Default is 4.

island_pop_size.description: The size of the population on each individual island. Default is 40.

generations.description: The total number of generations to run the evolution for. Default is 200.

migration_interval.description: The number of generations between migration events, where islands exchange individuals. Default is 20.

BOToolGv1_v3_2_0.name: bayesian_optimizer
BOToolGv1_v3_2_0.description:
Finds the global minimum using Bayesian Optimization (Gaussian Processes).
    Best for EXPENSIVE functions where you can only afford a few iterations (e.g. < 50).

    OUTPUT:
    - Returns best solution found.
    - Saves history to CSV.

    CRITICAL:
    - Uses `bayesian-optimization` package (v3.2.0+ compatible).
    - Read CSV using `csv_2_tup_tool` and INJECT data into `python_plotter`.

function_code.description: Python code 'def objective(x): ...' OR a standard function name (e.g., 'rastrigin', 'schwefel').

bounds.description: List of tuples e.g. [(-5, 5)]. Optional if using a standard function name.

output_filename.description: Filename for history CSV (e.g., 'bo_run1.csv'). Ends in .csv.

init_points.description: Number of random exploration steps before model starts. Default 5.

acq_type.description: Acquisition: 'ucb' (Upper Confidence Bound), 'ei' (Expected Improvement), or 'poi' (Probability Of Improvement). Default…

kappa.description: Exploration weight for UCB. Higher (e.g. 5.0)=Explore; Lower (e.g. 1.0)=Exploit. Default 2.5.

BOAnalysisTool.name: bo_analysis_tool
BOAnalysisTool.description:
Analyzes 'optimization_history.csv' from Bayesian Optimization.
    Diagnoses Exploration (Variance) vs Exploitation (Convergence).

csv_filename.description: Name of the history CSV file.
